title: Temporal cliques admit spanners of size O(n log n)
abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the theorem that every temporal clique on n vertices admits a temporal spanner with O(n log n) edges. A temporal clique is the complete graph on a finite vertex set whose edges carry natural-number time labels, locally injective (two edges sharing an endpoint have distinct labels); a temporal spanner is a set of edges in which every vertex reaches every other one by a journey with non-decreasing labels. The result is due to Casteigts, Peters and Schoeters (ICALP 2019, JCSS 2021); the formal proof follows the dismountability-only proof of Carnevale, Casteigts and Corsini (SAND 2025, §§2–4), which reduces cliques to bi-cliques and concludes with the one-sided dismountability of Angrick et al. (ESA 2024). The compared statements give an explicit bound of 2n⌈log₂ n⌉ + 4n edges and the asymptotic O(n log n) form with a bound function chosen uniformly for all cliques. The work is supervised by Arnaud Casteigts and Karine Altisen. Version 3 restores this statement, unchanged since version 1: version 2 registered by mistake another result of the same repository, the 7n bound of Baligács (2026), which now has its own entry. The proof is that of the library release alpha-0.2.0, in which the O(n log n) bound is an instance of a generic induction on cliques shared with the 7n bound.
